clue.text: When one is depressed it can be alarming

definitions.text: When one is depressed it can be alarming

parts.words: When one is depressed it can be alarming
parts.note: reads like a remark about low moods, but means a button that, once pressed down, sets a bell ringing

explanation.surface: A gloomy observation that feeling low can be frightening.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Depressed' looks emotional but means pushed down, and 'alarming' means ringing a bell rather than frightening.
explanation.definitionFit: A doorbell button is pressed down to make a bell ring, sounding an alert.

clue.text: This follower of immaculate miners' leader is retiring

definitions.text: This follower of immaculate miners' leader
definitions.meaning: immaculate is snow-white, and Snow White led the seven mining dwarfs; one of them is the shy one

explanation.surface: Some devoted follower of a spotless mining union boss is stepping down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retiring' looks like leaving work, but means shy; 'immaculate' is a cryptic way of saying Snow White, whose dwarfs worked in a mine.
explanation.definitionFit: Shy and self-conscious people tend to withdraw, and the shyest dwarf in the fairy tale is named for it.

clue.text: Operatic spectacles put up by Handel, we hear

definitions.text: Operatic spectacles put up by Handel, we hear

parts.words: Operatic spectacles put up by Handel, we hear
parts.note: seems to be about shows staged by the composer, but means opera glasses held up by a handle, the composer's name sounding like that word

explanation.surface: Operas staged by the composer Handel, so people say.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spectacles' suggests shows, but means glasses; Handel sounds like 'handle', the stick these opera glasses are held up by.
explanation.definitionFit: These eyeglasses on a long handle were fashionable at the theatre and opera house.

clue.text: Fellow the joke is on becomes peppery

indicators.note: in a down answer, one piece sitting on another comes above it

parts.note: a pun is a joke on words
a gent is a fellow or man

explanation.surface: A man who is the butt of a joke turns hot-tempered.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the joke is on' suggests mockery; in this down answer it puts PUN above GENT.
explanation.definitionFit: Hot spices give a sharp, biting taste or smell, so a peppery sauce is strongly flavoured.

clue.text: Skins pickles

definitions.meaning: skins as a verb means grazes, scratching the surface off

explanation.definitionFit: Grazes on the knee and tight fixes or jams are both words for mishaps.

clue.text: One six, say, can make silly mid-on duck!

indicators.note: silly suggests the letters of the fielding position are jumbled into nonsense

parts.note: a duck in cricket is a score of nothing, shaped like the letter O

explanation.surface: A cricket fielder at silly mid-on makes a nought, or a six.
explanation.walkthrough: 'silly' rearranges MIDON (from 'mid-on') into DOMIN; add O. Silly mid-on and mid-on are cricket fielding positions; a duck is a batter's score of zero. 'One six' is a tile's spots.
explanation.definitionFit: A tile marked with one spot and six spots is an example of a piece from the game of dominoes.

clue.text: Realms of party favourites?

parts.note: a do is a party
minions were favourites of a ruler

explanation.surface: A question whether a ruler's lands belong to his party favourites.
explanation.definitionFit: A sovereign's territories, lands ruled over, are kingdoms or realms.

clue.text: Cross with a black foot, say, on one side?

definitions.text: Cross with a black foot, say, on one side?

parts.words: Cross with a black foot, say, on one side?
parts.note: a cross is a mixed-blood person, one of whose parents might be a Blackfoot, a Native American people

explanation.surface: An angry person with a dark foot on one side.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cross' looks like angry; it means a person of mixed descent, and 'black foot' is the Blackfoot people of North America.
explanation.definitionFit: Spanish for a person of mixed European and Native American descent.

clue.text: Japanese play taking a long time to mount (over a year) gets a bouquet

indicators.note: in a down answer, over places the earlier pieces above the last

parts.note: No (Noh) is a classical Japanese drama

indicators.note: to mount means to climb, so in a down answer the word is read from the bottom up

parts.note: ages is a long time

explanation.surface: A Japanese drama takes more than a year to stage and is rewarded with flowers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to mount' turns AGES into SEGA; 'over' sets NOSEGA above Y. 'mount' suggests staging the play.
explanation.definitionFit: A small bunch of sweet-smelling flowers is a posy, given or worn like a corsage.

clue.text: Secure space for valuables

parts.note: a plain description of a locked, reinforced room where precious goods are kept, which also splits into words for safe and area

explanation.definitionFit: A vault-like chamber in a bank or house is built to keep jewels and money safe.

clue.text: Fair that will do twice

indicators.note: twice tells us to write the short exclamation two times over

parts.note: 'So!' can be said to mean that's enough, that will do

explanation.surface: A judgement that something is acceptable if repeated.
explanation.definitionFit: Middling or merely passable work is described as only average, neither good nor bad.

clue.text: Is an index essential to such art?

definitions.text: Is an index essential to such art?

parts.words: Is an index essential to such art?
parts.note: an index seems to be a book's list, but here it is the pointing digit used to daub colour in children's art

explanation.surface: A question about whether a reference list is needed for some kind of art.
explanation.walkthrough: 'index' pretends to be a book's alphabetical list; it is the index finger, the tool of this messy art.
explanation.definitionFit: Children often spread paint with their digits rather than a brush, a technique named after the hand part used.

clue.text: Understatement in T S Eliot play

indicators.note: play suggests the poet's initials and surname are toyed with and rearranged

explanation.surface: A remark that the poet T S Eliot wrote a restrained drama.
explanation.walkthrough: 'play' looks like one of Eliot's dramas but is the anagram signal for TSELIOT.
explanation.definitionFit: This figure of speech affirms by denying the opposite, as in 'not bad', a form of deliberate modesty in expression.

clue.text: To do needlework, colour yarn in this manner

definitions.meaning: to colour a yarn is to exaggerate a story, adding invented details

explanation.surface: Instructions for dyeing thread in a particular way when sewing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'yarn' suggests thread for sewing; here it is a tale, and 'colour' means embellish it.
explanation.definitionFit: Stitching decorative patterns on cloth, and also exaggerating a story with fanciful details.

clue.text: Name of place in which Cobbleigh kept the horse?

indicators.note: kept means one word holds the other inside it

parts.note: Uncle Tom Cobbleigh is the last rider named in the folk song Widecombe Fair, so the clue gives TOM
a pony is a small horse

explanation.surface: A question about the place where Old Uncle Tom Cobbleigh stabled the grey mare.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Widecombe Fair' is an English folk song in which a borrowed grey mare carries Uncle Tom Cobbleigh and friends.
explanation.definitionFit: Linguists use this term for a word naming a geographical location, such as a town or river.

clue.text: Note on kind of trumpet is almost a success

indicators.note: in a down answer, on puts the first piece above the second

parts.note: an ear trumpet is a kind of trumpet, jokingly an 'ear thing'

explanation.surface: A musical note played on some trumpet is nearly a triumph.
explanation.walkthrough: An ear trumpet is an old hearing aid, a horn held to the ear, so the clue calls it an 'ear thing'.
explanation.definitionFit: A narrow escape or a close finish that just fails is a close call.

clue.text: Having two necks, one was plucked. O, bother the mess!

definitions.text: Having two necks, one was plucked

indicators.note: making a mess of the words jumbles their letters

explanation.surface: An exasperated cry about a mess, after describing an odd stringed instrument.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mess' shuffles O and BOTHER; 'the' is a link. The definition describes an old lute with a second neck for bass strings.
explanation.definitionFit: This large Baroque lute had an extra neck carrying long bass strings, and was played by plucking.

clue.text: House with awful mould is becoming a crooked one

indicators.note: awful suggests the letters of the fungus are mangled

explanation.surface: A house with dreadful mould is turning into a bent wreck.
explanation.walkthrough: 'awful' rearranges MOULD into ODLUM. 'crooked' looks like bent or warped, but means criminal.
explanation.definitionFit: A thug or gangster is a criminal, someone not straight with the law.

clue.text: Prospect from square study?

parts.note: what one sees from the window of a study overlooking a town square, the view out

explanation.surface: A question about the view from a square-shaped study.
explanation.walkthrough: 'study' looks like a verb meaning learn; it is a room, and the view from its window is a prospect.
explanation.definitionFit: A view, or a forecast of what lies ahead, is a word for a prospect.

clue.text: Bandit chieftain who opened up Moby-Dick

definitions.meaning: the biblical outcast son of Abraham, ancestor of desert raiders, whose name came to mean a wild outlaw leader
Melville's novel begins with the narrator's line 'Call me ...', giving this name

explanation.surface: A marauding leader who began the story of the great white whale.
explanation.definitionFit: The narrator of Melville's whaling novel shares his name with Abraham's wandering son, father of nomad tribes.

clue.text: The whole or partial point E Germany makes?

indicators.note: partial means only part of the phrase is used, so the answer lies within

explanation.surface: A question about whether East Germany scores a full or half point.
explanation.walkthrough: 'E Germany' looks like East Germany, but supplies its letters only.
explanation.definitionFit: A whole number has no fractional part, so it is complete in itself.

clue.text: Herons flying over a Humberside town

indicators.note: in a down answer, over puts the jumbled birds above the final letter
flying suggests the birds scatter, rearranging their letters

explanation.surface: Wading birds flying over a seaside town in northern England.
explanation.walkthrough: Humberside was an English county around the Humber estuary; this resort lies on its North Sea coast.
explanation.definitionFit: This seaside resort on the Yorkshire coast lay within the former county of Humberside.

clue.text: Flag in narrow street leading to Italian course

indicators.note: in means one word is placed inside the other

parts.note: a lane is a narrow road or street
to flag is to tire and sag

explanation.surface: A flag hung in an alley on the way to an Italian dish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flag' looks like a banner; it is a verb meaning droop.
explanation.definitionFit: This layered pasta dish is served as a main course in Italian meals.

clue.text: Do its sufferers find their stairs too tricky?

definitions.text: Do its sufferers find their stairs too tricky?

indicators.note: tricky suggests the letters of the phrase are made awkward and rearranged

explanation.surface: A sympathetic question about whether people with a joint disease struggle with steps.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tricky' rearranges THEIRSTAIRSTOO; the whole clue also describes the illness, since stiff, painful joints make climbing stairs hard.
explanation.definitionFit: This degenerative joint disease causes stiff, painful knees and hips, so climbing steps is hard for patients.

clue.text: Unusual voice of a naval officer finding love

parts.note: LT is the abbreviation for lieutenant
love is nil in tennis, the letter O

explanation.surface: A sailor's officer has a strange singing voice when he falls in love.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is fair because a male voice in this high range is rare.
explanation.definitionFit: A high male singing range, above tenor, is uncommon among men.

clue.text: Detestable girl's squalling

parts.note: Di is a girl's name, so the girl's is DIS
squalling winds are gusting ones

explanation.surface: A complaint that a girl's screaming tantrum is hateful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'squalling' suggests a crying child, but here means blowing in squalls.
explanation.definitionFit: Something loathsome provokes revulsion, so it is sickening or repellent.

clue.text: Senor covering donkey — it's one that puffs

indicators.note: covering means one word wraps around the other

parts.note: SR is the abbreviation for senor, Spanish for Mr
moke is British slang for a donkey

explanation.surface: A Spanish gentleman riding a donkey, puffing as he goes.
explanation.walkthrough: MOKE is informal British slang for a donkey.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who inhales from cigarettes or pipes draws on them in puffs.

clue.text: Three-cornered' bar in the kitchen

parts.note: describes a metal rod bent into three sides that hangs in a kitchen and is struck to call people to eat

explanation.surface: A kitchen fitting described as a bar with three corners.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bar' suggests a counter or pub, but it is a metal rod bent into three sides, struck to summon diners.
explanation.definitionFit: A steel rod bent into a three-sided shape is rung as a dinner gong, as well as being a geometric figure.
